cards.title: Digital balance: Setting phone boundaries that stick
facts: Smartphones are pocket slot machines engineered with infinite feeds and variable notifications to keep your attention captive.
Setting intentional physical and temporal boundaries reclaims 3 to 4 hours of your day for real-world passions, fitness, and sleep.
do: Establish a 'phone curfew' by charging your phone outside your bedroom 60 minutes before bedtime
Turn your phone screen to Grayscale (black & white) mode to eliminate visual dopamine rewards from icons
Use app limits with passcode locks managed by yourself or a parent to enforce realistic cut-offs
dont: Never keep your smartphone right beside your pillow while sleeping
Never check your notifications within the first 15 minutes of waking up in the morning

myths.statement: Using your phone for 7 hours a day on social media has zero impact on your academic or mental performance.
myths.truth: Heavy screen time is clinically linked to attention fragmentation, decreased reading comprehension, and heightened anxiety.

quiz.q: What simple screen display adjustment removes the addictive visual appeal of app icons and notifications?
options: Switching screen display to Grayscale (black and white)
quiz.explanation: Grayscale strips away the vibrant red and orange notification badges engineered by app designers to hook attention.

rubric.point: Switch phone screen to grayscale mode and place it in another room during study and sleep hours
rubric.note: Reduces visual dopamine hooks and physical accessibility.

rubric.point: Set daily 30-minute hard app limits on video platforms using built-in digital wellbeing tools
rubric.note: Automates behavioral boundaries through software timers.
rubric.keys: set 30 min app limit|digital wellbeing tools

rubric.point: Substitute scrolling with hands-on physical activities: guitar practice, outdoor cycling, or board games
rubric.note: Replaces passive consumption with active engagement.
rubric.keys: substitute real activities|guitar practice|outdoor cycling

blame parents for having a phone

cards.title: The notification diet: Silence the synthetic noise
facts: Every notification chime triggers a cortisol and dopamine spike that interrupts your brain's flow state and takes 23 minutes to fully recover.
Most notifications are not urgent messages from friends; they are corporate algorithms begging you to reopen their apps.
do: Turn off all notifications for shopping, gaming, video streaming, and news apps immediately
Keep sound/vibration alerts enabled ONLY for direct phone calls and 1-on-1 human messages
Schedule batch notification summaries twice a day rather than receiving real-time interruptions
dont: Never leave push notifications turned on for casual mobile games or shopping discounts
Never allow flashing LED notification lights to disturb your study desk

myths.statement: You must keep all app notifications turned on so you don't miss breaking world news or flash sales.
myths.truth: Push notifications are advertising channels, not emergency alarms. Turning off 90% of notifications restores hours of deep daily focus.

quiz.q: How long does it take the human brain to regain deep focus after being interrupted by a single phone chime?
quiz.explanation: Cognitive science shows task switching and attentional residue require over 20 minutes to return to deep concentration.

scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Open system settings and permanently disable notifications for all games, shopping, and social feeds
rubric.note: Eliminates non-essential algorithmic distractions.
rubric.keys: disable non-essential notifications|turn off game alerts|shopping alerts off

rubric.point: Enable 'Do Not Disturb' or Focus Mode during dedicated study blocks
rubric.note: Shields working memory during deep study sessions.
rubric.keys: enable do not disturb|focus mode|study block

rubric.point: Keep alerts active only for urgent direct calls from family members
rubric.note: Preserves genuine emergency channels.
rubric.keys: family calls only|emergency channel

dangerous: check phone at every single buzz
throw phone at the wall
leave all notifications on full volume

cards.title: Mastering gaming limits: Sunk cost and stopping cues
facts: Modern competitive and online games deliberately eliminate 'stopping cues' (like chapters or quarters) to keep players locked in 'just one more match'.
The 'sunk cost fallacy' tricks you into grinding hours for virtual armor or rank points that have zero utility outside the game server.
do: Set a clear end time BEFORE booting up a game (e.g., 'I will play exactly two matches or 45 minutes')
Use an external physical alarm clock placed across the room rather than an easily dismissed phone banner
Treat gaming as a delicious dessert earned after finishing homework and exercise, not the main course of your day
dont: Never play online games past midnight on school nights
Never spend real family money or allowance on randomized digital weapon crates

myths.statement: Professional esports players play 16 hours a day without sleeping, so doing the same is good training.
myths.truth: Top esports athletes follow strict physical workouts, sleep hygiene, nutrition, and mental health protocols to maintain reaction speed.

quiz.q: What is a 'stopping cue' in digital media and games?
options: A button that turns off the internet
A natural transition point (like the end of a chapter or match) that reminds you to pause and re-evaluate your time
quiz.explanation: Stopping cues signal natural closure; games remove them intentionally to foster endless automatic play.

rubric.point: Recognize the 'tilt' and sunk-cost trap: playing tired leads to worse gameplay and ruined tomorrow sleep
rubric.note: Recognizes emotional tilt and cognitive fatigue.

rubric.point: Firmly log off the console, power down the display, and head to bed
rubric.note: Enforces discipline over impulse.
rubric.keys: log off console|power down|go to bed

rubric.note: Puts gaming status in perspective.

cards.title: Escaping doom-scrolling: Breaking the catastrophe news loop
facts: Doom-scrolling is the compulsive habit of continuously scrolling through distressing, sensationalist disaster news and outrage online.
Social media algorithms heavily favor terrifying headlines because human survival instincts prioritize threat detection above all else.
do: Notice the bodily sensation of doom-scrolling: tight chest, clenched jaw, shallow breathing, and rising dread
Set a hard 10-minute daily timer for checking current events and get news from curated, reliable print/weekly summaries
Practice 'scroll-stopping': physically stand up, stretch your arms, and look out the window at green trees
dont: Never consume sensationalist crime or disaster headlines right before closing your eyes to sleep
Never share unverified terrifying breaking news videos on WhatsApp without fact-checking

myths.statement: Doom-scrolling through catastrophic news for three hours a day makes you a responsible, well-informed citizen.
myths.truth: Compulsive doom-scrolling causes learned helplessness, severe anxiety, and emotional paralysis without helping a single victim.

quiz.q: Why do social media algorithms consistently serve catastrophic, negative news to your feed?
options: Because only bad things happen in the universe
Because threatening news hooks human survival attention and keeps eyes on screen longer for ad revenue
Because algorithms want you to be safe
quiz.explanation: Fear and outrage generate the highest engagement metrics, which algorithms exploit for commercial profit.

scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize the doom-scrolling loop, physically place the phone on the desk, and stand up
rubric.note: Breaks the physical trance state.
rubric.keys: break doom scrolling trance|put phone on desk|stand up

rubric.point: Drink a glass of water and replace digital dread with calming physical reality (reading a book or deep breathing)
rubric.note: Re-grounds the nervous system in immediate safety.
rubric.keys: drink water|calming reality|deep breathing

rubric.point: Delete sensationalist algorithm-driven news aggregators from the phone
rubric.note: Removes the source of toxic information overload.
rubric.keys: delete news aggregators|curate information diet

cards.title: Phone-free meals: Reclaiming human connection at the dinner table
facts: 'Phubbing' (phone snubbing) is the act of ignoring the living people sitting right across from you to stare at a glowing glass screen.
Family meal tables without digital screens are the single strongest predictor of adolescent emotional resilience and vocabulary development.
do: Keep the dining table a sacred 100% phone-free zone for the entire family
Place all phones in a basket or on a side table on silent mode during dinner
Ask engaging table conversation questions: 'What was the funniest thing that happened today?'
dont: Never scroll social feeds, text friends, or watch YouTube videos while eating meals with others
Never leave your phone face-up on the dining table where flashing screens interrupt conversations

myths.statement: Having your phone sitting face-up on the dinner table has zero effect on conversation quality if it is on silent.
myths.truth: Studies prove the mere visible presence of a phone on a table reduces conversation depth, empathy, and interpersonal trust.

quiz.q: What is the term used by psychologists for ignoring the people right in front of you in favor of your smartphone?
quiz.explanation: Phubbing damages personal relationships and signals to loved ones that a screen is more important than their presence.

situations: During dinner with family at {at}, {name}'s phone chimes with non-urgent Instagram comments, and {name} reaches to unlock it.

scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Leave the phone untouched and place it face-down away from the dinner table
rubric.note: Prioritizes immediate family presence over digital pings.
rubric.keys: leave phone untouched|place face down away|prioritize family

rubric.point: Engage actively in conversation with family members about their day
rubric.note: Cultivates genuine interpersonal connection.
rubric.keys: engage in family conversation|listen actively

rubric.point: Suggest a family rule where everyone deposits devices in a basket during meal times

cards.title: Deep study focus: The Pomodoro technique and phone separation
facts: Human multitasking is a neurological myth; the brain cannot focus on two complex tasks simultaneously, it merely switches back and forth frantically.
Studying with a phone buzzing nearby reduces effective IQ and doubles the hours required to memorize textbook material.
do: Use the Pomodoro Technique: 25 minutes of 100% distraction-free study followed by a strict 5-minute break
Physically place your phone in another room or inside a closed drawer while studying
Use website blockers on your computer to lock distracting entertainment portals during homework hours
dont: Never attempt to study for difficult exams with a video stream playing in the corner of your screen
Never respond to text messages during active 25-minute study sprints

myths.statement: Gen Z brains have evolved to multitask effortlessly between calculus homework, music, and group texting at the same time.
myths.truth: Human brain architecture has not changed. Multitasking creates superficial learning, frequent errors, and cognitive exhaustion.

quiz.q: What is the core structure of the classic 'Pomodoro Technique' for academic study?
options: Studying for 10 hours straight without food
25 minutes of single-task focused study followed by a 5-minute restorative break
quiz.explanation: The 25/5 rhythm matches optimal human attention spans and prevents mental fatigue during revision.

rubric.note: Implements Pomodoro focus sprint.
rubric.keys: 25 minute timer|pomodoro sprint|single task study

rubric.point: Reward yourself with a 5-minute stretch or walk after completing the focus block

rubric.keys: 5 min stretch break|restorative pause

cards.title: Resisting microtransactions: Virtual cosmetics vs real wealth
facts: Free-to-play mobile games employ behavioral dark patterns, fake countdowns, and peer pressure to sell virtual gun skins and dance emotes.
Spending real rupee money on pixels inside a game yields zero tangible value; when the game server shuts down, all skins vanish permanently.
do: Set a firm rule: Never spend real currency on cosmetic skins that do not alter core gameplay
If you want to make an in-game purchase, wait a mandatory 72-hour cooling-off period before deciding
Never memorize or store parental credit cards or UPI details inside app stores
dont: NEVER secretly use a parent's credit card or banking OTP to purchase game passes
NEVER fall for scams promising 'free diamonds' or 'free V-bucks' in exchange for account passwords

myths.statement: Buying rare limited-edition weapon skins in online games is a smart financial investment that will make you wealthy later.
myths.truth: Game terms of service forbid real-money account trading, and game economies crash regularly. Virtual cosmetics are pure consumable expenses.

quiz.q: What happens to all your purchased in-game weapon skins and character outfits when the game developer closes the game servers?
options: They get transferred to your bank account
They disappear completely and permanently with zero compensation
They turn into real physical clothes
quiz.explanation: You do not own virtual items; you merely hold a temporary, revocable license that expires when servers shut down.

cards.title: App age ratings: Protecting developing brains from adult content
facts: Age ratings on games and apps (PEGI 18, ESRB M, 13+) exist because developing adolescent brains process extreme violence, horror, and sexual themes differently than adults.
Premature exposure to hyper-graphic violence and adult themes desensitizes emotional empathy and triggers chronic sleep disturbances.
do: Check app and game age ratings (12+, 16+, 18+) before downloading new titles
Respect age restrictions: they are designed by neuroscientists and psychologists to safeguard adolescent mental development
Talk openly with parents if you accidentally stumble across graphic, violent, or disturbing web content
dont: Never fake your date of birth to bypass 18+ restrictions on adult gambling or dating apps
Never peer-pressure younger siblings or juniors into watching graphic horror movies or adult games

myths.statement: Age ratings on video games are just pointless suggestions made by boring adults with no real scientific basis.
myths.truth: Age ratings reflect clinical research on cognitive readiness, emotional trauma processing, and addiction vulnerability in youth.

quiz.q: What does an '18+' or 'Mature' rating on a video game indicate?
options: The game is suitable for kindergarten children
The game contains graphic violence, mature sexual content, or intense themes unsuitable for developing adolescents
The game takes 18 hours to complete
quiz.explanation: Mature ratings warn that content requires adult emotional maturity to process without psychological distress.

cards.title: The midnight rule: Never post or message when tired or angry
facts: Late at night, your prefrontal cortex is depleted, your inhibitions drop, and emotional impulses dominate your judgment.
Frantic midnight texts, impulsive romantic confessions, and angry comments posted after 11 PM account for 80% of digital regrets.
do: Enforce the 'Midnight Rule': Never send a sensitive, emotional, or confrontational text after 10 PM
Save passionate, angry messages as drafts and sleep on them; review them with fresh eyes tomorrow morning
Put your phone away across the room when settling in for bed
dont: Never hit 'Send' on a heated argument while lying in bed in the dark
Never post personal vulnerability rants on public social media stories late at night

myths.statement: If someone insults you online at midnight, you must reply within 60 seconds or you look weak.
myths.truth: Late-night replies look reckless and reactive. Replying with cool, calculated composure the next morning shows mastery and power.

Save the message as a draft, sleep on it, and review it in daylight before deciding to send

quiz.explanation: Sleeping on emotional drafts allows prefrontal executive function to restore, preventing embarrassing relationship catastrophes.

cards.title: Muting the chaos: Surviving 50-person group chats
facts: Large school, sports, and social group chats generate hundreds of meaningless memes, stickers, and side chatter every hour.
Feeling obligated to read every single group chat bubble creates continuous background anxiety and drains battery and study time.
do: Mute large group chats permanently or for 1 year, checking them on YOUR schedule once or twice a day
Turn off auto-download for photos and videos in WhatsApp to save phone storage and cellular data
Use group chats for functional logistics (homework questions, event times), not endless 24/7 banter
dont: Never feel guilty for missing 200 unread memes in a school chat group
Never post large chain letters, spam forwarding messages, or unverified rumors into group chats

myths.statement: You have a social obligation to read every single message and respond with an emoji in every group chat you belong to.
myths.truth: Group chats are broadcast channels, not private conversations. Constantly checking group chats fractures your attention span.

quiz.explanation: Disabling media auto-download stops thousands of useless media files from automatically filling your phone storage.

cards.title: Zombie walking: Why staring at screens while walking is deadly
facts: 'Distracted walking' while texting or watching videos narrows your peripheral vision by 90%, blinding you to open manholes, stairs, and traffic.
Pedestrians using phones have a 4x higher risk of collision with motor vehicles, electric scooters, and train platforms.
do: Keep your phone safely in your pocket or backpack whenever your feet are moving outdoors
If you must answer an urgent message, step completely aside against a building wall and stop moving
Never wear noise-cancelling headphones over both ears while crossing busy roads or railway tracks
dont: NEVER cross a road, pedestrian zebra crossing, or railway track while looking at a phone screen
NEVER walk down school staircases with your eyes glued to a mobile video

myths.statement: Walking while texting is completely safe because peripheral vision automatically alerts you to all oncoming traffic.
myths.truth: Cognitive tunneling blinds distracted pedestrians. People staring at screens regularly walk straight into open drains, poles, and moving cars.

quiz.q: What happens to your field of situational awareness when you walk while looking down at a smartphone?
options: It narrows by up to 90%, leaving you oblivious to approaching vehicles and road hazards
It makes your reflexes twice as fast
quiz.explanation: Looking down creates severe cognitive tunneling, rendering you completely blind to environmental hazards.

cards.title: Intentional viewing: Taming the infinite video algorithm

Search specifically for what you want to learn, watch it, and then close the browser tab
Ask yourself every 20 minutes: 'Did I choose to watch this, or did an algorithm pick it for me?'

Never leave video streams running in the background all night while falling asleep

myths.truth: Algorithms have one single commercial objective: maximize time-on-screen to sell more advertisements, regardless of content quality.

cards.title: The weekend digital detox: Rediscovering the physical world
facts: Taking a 24-hour break from screens on a Saturday or Sunday resets your dopamine baseline, lowers cortisol, and sparks creative clarity.
Unplugged time frees up hours for deep conversations, outdoor sports, cooking, reading physical books, and tactile creativity.
do: Choose a specific 24-hour window (e.g., Saturday 6 PM to Sunday 6 PM) for your digital detox
Inform family and close friends in advance: 'I am taking a screen-free day, call my home landline or parent if urgent'
Plan tactile physical activities in advance: hiking, sketching, board games, cycling, or baking
dont: Never treat a screen-free day as punishment; view it as a luxurious retreat for your brain
Never keep your phone in your pocket during a detox day; lock it in a desk drawer

myths.statement: Taking one day off from your smartphone will cause your social relationships to completely collapse.
myths.truth: Real friends respect digital detoxes. Disconnecting for 24 hours rejuvenates your mental energy and deepens real-world presence.

cards.title: Vanity metrics: Why follower counts do not equal human worth
facts: Social media 'likes', 'views', and follower counts are vanity metrics engineered by ad tech companies to trigger slot-machine dopamine loops.
Tying your self-esteem to fluctuating social metrics makes you emotionally vulnerable to internet algorithms and anonymous trolls.
do: Remember: A post with 5 likes is not inferior to a post with 50,000 likes; algorithms measure virality, not truth or beauty
Turn off public like counts in Instagram settings to liberate yourself from metric anxiety
Focus on the quality of your real-world character: Are you loyal, trustworthy, hardworking, and kind?
dont: Never delete a creative drawing or essay you love just because it didn't get enough online likes
Never engage in dangerous stunts, pranks, or humiliating acts to chase viral views

myths.statement: The number of followers you have on Instagram or YouTube is an accurate measure of how smart, beautiful, and successful you are.
myths.truth: Follower counts measure sensationalism, algorithmic favor, or paid promotion—never wisdom, integrity, or true happiness.

quiz.q: What setting on major social platforms helps disconnect your self-worth from engagement approval?
options: Hiding like and view counts on posts
quiz.explanation: Hiding like counts removes the public scorecard, allowing you to share and consume content without constant comparison anxiety.

cards.title: Spotting screen addiction: Recognizing the red flags
facts: Digital addiction is characterized by loss of control over screen use, withdrawal irritability when offline, and neglect of essential life duties.
Catching digital overuse early through self-assessment prevents severe academic failure, physical posture degradation, and social isolation.
do: Watch for red flags: lying about screen time, feeling restless/angry when disconnected, neglecting meals and hygiene
Take an honest weekly self-inventory: Are your grades slipping? Are you sleeping less than 7 hours? Are real friendships fading?
Ask for help from parents, school counselors, or clinics (like SHUT clinic at NIMHANS) if you cannot stop alone
dont: Never steal money, lie to family, or skip school to feed an online gaming habit
Never dismiss friends or parents when they express loving concern about your device obsession

myths.statement: Because everyone carries a smartphone, it is scientifically impossible to become addicted to screens.
myths.truth: Behavioral addictions hijack the exact same dopamine reward circuits as chemical dependencies. Clinical screen addiction is recognized globally by WHO.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a recognized clinical warning sign of behavioral screen addiction?
options: Charging your phone when the battery reaches 10%
Experiencing intense anger, agitation, or panic whenever the phone is temporarily removed
Using a phone calculator for math homework
quiz.explanation: Severe emotional distress or aggression when separated from devices indicates psychological dependency.

rubric.note: Replaces defensive hostility with understanding.

cards.title: Device hygiene: Cleaning screens safely and protecting hardware
facts: Smartphone screens harbor more bacteria than a toilet seat; regular gentle cleaning prevents acne, skin infections, and device decay.
Taking physical care of your digital tools (cables, keyboards, screens) extends their lifespan and teaches financial stewardship.
do: Clean glass screens using a dry microfiber cloth; lightly dampen with 70% isopropyl alcohol for disinfection
Never spray liquids, soapy water, or harsh household window cleaners directly onto device ports or screens
Gently coil charging cables in wide loops; never bend or yank cords sharply from the plug head
dont: Never eat crumbly snacks directly over laptop keyboards or drop sticky juice onto game controllers
Never use metal safety pins or needles to dig dirt out of phone charging ports

myths.statement: Washing your smartphone screen with running tap water and dish soap is the best way to sanitize it.
myths.truth: Water and soap penetrate microphone meshes and speaker grilles, destroying internal motherboards. Use dry microfiber and alcohol wipes only.

quiz.q: What is the safest material to use when wiping dust, oil, and fingerprints off a glass smartphone or tablet screen?
options: A clean microfiber cloth (like the ones used for spectacles)
quiz.explanation: Microfiber lifts skin oils and dust without scratching delicate anti-fingerprint oleophobic glass coatings.

cards.title: Consumer to creator: Using tech to build, compose, and solve
facts: The greatest tragedy of the smartphone era is reducing a miraculous supercomputer into a passive entertainment pacifier.
Transforming from a passive digital consumer into an active digital creator (coding, 3D modeling, music production, writing) builds true agency.
do: Shift your screen ratio: For every 1 hour of passive video consumption, spend 1 hour actively building or creating
Learn foundational digital creation tools: Python programming, Canva/Figma visual design, Audacity audio editing
Use the internet to publish educational tutorials, open-source code, digital art, or community journalism
dont: Never allow technology to keep you entirely in the role of a passive, paying customer
Never assume that creating software or digital media is reserved only for geniuses

myths.statement: Smartphones and computers are designed exclusively for playing games, scrolling memes, and streaming movies.
myths.truth: Computers are bicycles for the mind. They are the most powerful creative, scientific, and enterprise instruments ever invented.

quiz.q: What characterizes an active 'digital creator' mindset compared to a passive 'digital consumer'?
options: Watching 10 hours of video game walkthroughs per day
Using digital software to write code, design artwork, compose music, or solve community problems
Buying every new phone model on launch day
Commenting angry emojis on celebrity pages
quiz.explanation: Creators leverage technology as an expressive tool to solve problems, build assets, and share original value.

cards.title: Screen ergonomics: Defeating 'Text Neck' and the 20-20-20 eye rule
facts: Bending your neck forward at a 60-degree angle to look down at a phone places 27 kilograms of crushing gravitational pressure on your cervical spine.
Staring at nearby digital screens reduces blink rates by 50%, causing dry eye syndrome, ocular strain, and progressive myopia.
do: Apply the 20-20-20 Rule: Every 20 minutes, look at an object at least 20 feet (6 meters) away for 20 seconds
Hold your phone up closer to eye level rather than dropping your chin to your chest ('bring phone to eyes, not eyes to phone')
Keep computer screens an arm's length away with the top of the monitor aligned with your eye line
dont: Never hunch over a laptop in bed with your spine bent like a folded taco
Never read smartphones in a pitch-black bedroom without ambient room lighting

myths.statement: Slouching over your phone with your neck bent down for 6 hours a day causes no permanent physical spinal damage.
myths.truth: 'Text Neck' causes premature spinal disc degeneration, chronic headaches, pinched nerves, and permanent postural hunching.

quiz.q: What does the famous ophthalmological '20-20-20 Rule' prescribe for screen users?
options: Spend 20 hours on screens, 20 minutes outside, 20 rupees on drops
Every 20 minutes, look at an object 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds
quiz.explanation: Looking 20 feet away relaxes the eye's ciliary muscles, immediately preventing eye strain and fatigue.
